chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fadhal and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, all together said:
We presented the Book of Obligations (Inheritance) from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), so he said: 'It is correct.'

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida, the eighth Imam (AS)
key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (AS)
key_terms.الْفَرَائِضِ: Obligations or shares, specifically referring to inheritance law

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Rida verify the authenticity of the inheritance book attributed to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the rigorous methodology of hadith authentication in Shia scholarship, where later Imams served as the ultimate validators of earlier transmitted texts. By confirming the 'Fara'id' book attributed to Imam Ali (AS), Imam al-Rida (AS) not only verified its textual integrity but also established the continuity of the Ahl al-Bayt's authoritative role in interpreting divine law. This validation underscores the reliability of the transmission chain (isnad) and the specific inheritance jurisprudence preserved within the Imams' teachings.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazal and Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, both together said,
‘We presented a book of the Obligations, from Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is correct’.
